note:
staging takes 1.5.1. Two releases are crossed, 1.4.5 to 1.5.1, and 1.5.0 is
skipped. 1.5.0 was published to this channel on 2026-09-08 and applied nowhere:
its own apply failed on every claw at a check for a file the same run declined to
write, which is the defect 1.5.1 fixes. Everything 1.5.0 carried is in this
payload, so nothing is lost by skipping it and no skipped release carries a
landing section anybody has to read.

The releases: 1.5.1 declares class fix, disruption quiet. No core floor moves.
Codex stays at 0.147.0 and Claude stays at 2.1.227, the same values 1.4.5 and
1.5.0 both declared.

RIDE THIS ATTENDED AND PASS --now. A claw that already carries the mail
gatekeeper classifies every release as core-moving, whatever the release
declares, and defers it to the quiet window of 04:00 to 06:00 local. Measured on
staging at 12:05Z on 2026-09-08: a scheduled tick read this claw's own state and
answered "deferred to the quiet window" for a release declaring quiet. The cause
is the mail service's own account. It sits in claw-members, which is what lets it
put a message on the bus, and the updater reads claw-members to ask whether any
person's core is below the floor. The account has no core, so it reads as a
person who is below it. Each of the other two arms of that classification was
asked on its own and both pass on this box. This is a defect of the 1.5.x family
and it is not fixed here. --now is the flag the rail already carries for a person
standing at the box.

The box, measured on staging at 11:38Z and again at 12:06Z:
claw-members holds jeremiah and email-gate. The person's persistent-session core
is installed and reads 2.1.227, and their per-task core reads 0.147.0. Both meet
the floors this release declares, so no person on this claw is below one. The
per-task core's companion host is present. email-gate is the service account the
failed 1.5.0 run created and it is not a person.

The same reading for what this release writes. This claw already carries the mail
gatekeeper: the email-gate account, the tree under /srv/connections/email-gatekeeper,
a routing table with an empty self, and the service enabled and running with no
provider key. /etc/commonclaw/email-gatekeeper.env is absent, which is the one
file 1.5.1 adds. This apply writes that file, adopts everything else as it
stands, and does not restart a service that is already running.

The claw records 1.4.5 with last_verdict "apply failed", failing_version 1.5.0
and one failure counted of three. A newer version starts that count again, so
1.5.1 is offered with a clean count.

This release installs a mail service under its own system account and no claw
carries a provider key for it. A firm puts that key into its own machine vault
with install-email-provider-key.sh and makes the address once with
email inbox create. Until the key is there the service reaches no provider, and
the apply says so in notes that name both doors.

A firm's email orchestrator is a separate thing and it does not arrive here. It
is launched from the email skill in the open library, which writes the firm's
communication runbook and then records where it put it with
email self set runbook. This payload carries no skill: the fleet manifest
declares claw-ops alone and the assembler names claw-ops alone.

An update run by hand no longer reports every other member's git identity as
missing. The people phase reached each member from wherever the operator was
standing, and one member cannot look inside another member's home, so the read
died there and the run said the identity was absent. From this release those git
calls stand at the root of the filesystem. Ride from there.
